title: Interruptible streaming fragmenter and event coalescer for Python SDK
creator: Ava Chen
description: Provide an ergonomic Python SDK primitive that yields partial streaming chat outputs as stable, idempotent fragments and surfaces typed events (token, delta, metadata, checkpoint, end, error). The primitive should be interrupt-safe (CTRL-C / SIGINT), support retrying only the minimal retryable fragment(s), and provide backpressure hints and simple adapter hooks for application-level event coalescing and checkpoints.
background: Customers integrating streaming chat often struggle with: (1) producing partial UI updates without duplicating tokens on resume, (2) handling user interrupts (Ctrl-C / cancel) gracefully, (3) deciding which parts of a stream are safe to retry, and (4) reconciling a high-volume token stream with application rendering and telemetry. Current SDK examples scatter these concerns across sample code and apps, causing inconsistencies and bugs in production integrations.
proposed_solution:
Introduce a StreamingFragmenter API that:
- Emits typed events: 'token', 'delta', 'meta', 'checkpoint', 'end', 'error'.
- Converts raw server SSE/WS streaming rows into idempotent fragments with a fragment_id and sequence range.
- Exposes a Python async iterator (and sync adapter) yielding Event objects in-order.
- Supports a .checkpoint() call (user or automatic) that marks consumer-visible stable state; only fragments after the last checkpoint are eligible for retry on transient failures.
- Provides a RetryPolicy configuration: retryable_statuses, max_fragment_retries, backoff.
- Offers backpressure controls: max_buffer_tokens, flush_on_tokens, flush_on_time_ms.
- Has built-in signal/interrupt handler integration to allow safe cancellation that still commits last checkpoint and returns a resumable token/receipt.
design_decisions:
1) Representing events as tuple-like typed events rather than nested dicts to keep memory footprint low.
2) Expose both async iterator API and a ContextManager helper (.stream_as_context()) for easier resource cleanup on interrupts.
3) Keep fragment ids monotonically increasing per-session so checkpoints are simple integers.
4) Make checkpoint semantics explicit: a checkpoint guarantees consumer-visible result will not be retried; fragments before checkpoint are durable and not replayed.
tradeoffs:
- Explicit checkpoints require developers to think about consistency; automatic checkpoints risk masking correctness issues but are available as a convenience.
- Coalescing tokens into deltas reduces app render churn but slightly increases per-event latency.
- Implementing fragment-level retries increases complexity in the SDK runtime and tests but reduces wasted tokens and developer work to deduplicate responses on resume.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (prototype): implement StreamingFragmenter core parsing and token->fragment grouping, simple async iterator, unit tests for event ordering and checkpoint semantics. (ETA 2 weeks)
Phase 2 (integrations): add signal handling, retry policy, backpressure knobs, sync adapter, and example notebooks. (ETA 2 weeks)
Phase 3 (hardening): load tests, telemetry, docs/recipes, API reviews, PRs, and prepare for release. (ETA 1 week)
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes StreamingFragmenter with documented async iterator and sync adapter
Tokens and deltas are yielded in-order with stable fragment_id attached
Checkpoint call prevents previously committed fragments from being retried on transient errors
Interrupting via SIGINT triggers cleanup and returns a resumable receipt (session_id + last_checkpoint)
Integration tests demonstrate retry only replays fragments after last checkpoint and does not duplicate committed output
Bench tests show coalescing latency < 30ms additional on p50 and memory usage within budget
tests: unit: event ordering with interleaved meta/delta/token messages
unit: checkpoint semantics - no replay of pre-checkpoint fragments
integration: simulated network drop triggers fragment-level retry path
integration: CTRL-C during stream commits checkpoint and produces resumable receipt
perf: end-to-end rendering with flush_on_tokens under load
rollout_plan: Merge behind an opt-in flag 'streaming_fragmenter:beta' on SDK main. Publish alpha docs and example app. Invite 3 internal teams (console, docs playground, solutions) to test. Collect telemetry (fragment replay counts, checkpoint frequency, interrupt occurrences) for two weeks. Flip default if metrics and bugs are acceptable.
telemetry: Emit events: fragment_created, fragment_committed (checkpoint), fragment_replayed, stream_interrupted, fragment_retry_failed. Track fragment size distribution and time-to-first-checkpoint. Add sampling to token events to avoid high cardinality.
